hints: Look carefully at what the ventricular volume line is about to do at P and at R. At P it is high and about to fall sharply, at R it is low and about to rise again.
Remember valves close to prevent backflow when pressure on the downstream side becomes higher. Think about which valve must shut to start ventricular contraction, and which must shut to end it.
walkthrough:
**Read the graph like a story**

Hello, let's start simply. The y-axis is volume of blood inside the ventricles.

When the line goes down, blood is leaving the ventricles. When the line goes up, blood is filling the ventricles.

**Work out what happens at P**

P is at the end of atrial systole and the very start of ventricular systole. The ventricles are full, and they are about to contract.

As ventricular muscle contracts, ventricular pressure quickly rises above atrial pressure. This slams the atrioventricular valves shut to stop blood flowing back into the atria. So the atrioventricular valve at P closes.

**Work out what happens at R**

R is at the end of ventricular systole. The volume is at its lowest because most blood has been ejected into the arteries. The ventricles are about to relax for diastole.

As the ventricles relax, ventricular pressure falls below the pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery. This causes the semilunar valves to shut to stop blood flowing back into the ventricles. So the semilunar valve at R closes.

options.A: Perfect. AV valve closes at P to prevent atrial backflow when ventricles contract, and semilunar valve closes at R to prevent arterial backflow when ventricles relax.
options.B: The first part is right, the AV valve does close at P, but the semilunar valve does not open at R. At R ejection has finished and pressure is falling, so it closes.
options.C: The second part is right, the semilunar valve does close at R, but the AV valve does not open at P. At P the ventricles are full and starting to contract, so it closes.
options.D: Neither valve opens here. Both P and R are closing points to prevent backflow, first of the AV valves, then of the semilunar valves.
